x-invariants: open has three modes. Absent, the dialog keeps its own state: it starts closed and a tap on the trigger opens it. A `{"@path"}` binding makes the data model the state: the dialog follows it, and the trigger and the user's close write it. A literal boolean is shown as given: the dialog refuses to be closed by the user.
The trigger is drawn in place and opens the dialog on a tap, also when it has a click of its own, which still runs. Without a trigger nothing is drawn in place.

A tap on confirmButton or dismissButton closes the dialog and sends no onDismissRequest; the child's own click still runs. A close by the user (the scrim, back or Escape) on a bound dialog writes false to the path, then sends onDismissRequest. On a literal dialog it only sends onDismissRequest.

M3ModalNavigationDrawer.description: Material 3 modal navigation drawer: a sheet that slides over the content from the start edge.
x-invariants: open has two modes. Absent, the drawer keeps its own state: it starts closed, opens on an edge swipe or on a tap on the `navigationIcon` of a top app bar in content, and closes on the scrim, back, a swipe or a click on an M3NavigationDrawerItem. A `{"@path"}` binding makes the data model the state: the drawer follows it, and the actions above write it. A literal boolean is shown as given: the drawer refuses to be moved by the user and does not take system back.
A close by the user (scrim, back or swipe) on a bound drawer writes false to the path, then sends onDismissRequest. On a literal drawer a scrim tap or a swipe only sends onDismissRequest.
Needs a bounded height: in a parent that gives none, such as a vertically scrolling column, it shows an error box instead of the page.

M3Scaffold.description: Material 3 scaffold: the page frame that places a top bar, a bottom bar, a snackbar host and a floating action around the content.
x-invariants: The content is laid out inside the bars, so it is never under them; a top app bar in topBar sees the scroll of the content, which is the only way M3TopAppBarScroll and M3CollapsingTopAppBarScroll take effect.
Needs a bounded height: in a parent that gives none, such as a vertically scrolling column, it shows an error box instead of the page.

M3SecondaryTabRow.description: Material 3 secondary tab row: a row of M3Tab children, of which exactly one is selected, with a full width indicator under the selected tab.
x-invariants: value holds the key of the selected tab and must be a `{"@path"}` binding; a click on a tab writes that tab's `key` to it, then runs the tab's own `onClick`. With a literal value the tabs are disabled, so nothing is written and no action is sent. A value that matches no tab key selects none and shows no indicator. The indicator follows only a literal `key` of a listed id that has rendered, with every id before it rendered too; otherwise it is not shown.
List the tabs by id in `content`; their order is the tab order. A row cannot hold anything but M3Tab.

M3SegmentedButton.description: Material 3 segmented button: one segment of an M3SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow or an M3MultiChoiceSegmentedButtonRow.

The button has no `value`: the row owns the selection, and a button is selected when the row's value matches key. A click updates the row's value, then runs onClick.
The button is disabled while the row's value is not a `{"@path"}` binding.

List the buttons by id in `content`; their order is the segment order. A row cannot hold anything but M3SegmentedButton.

M3Snackbar.description: Material 3 snackbar: a short message strip with an optional action, drawn where it is placed.
x-invariants: Stateless: it never hides itself and has no timeout. To show a message that goes away by itself, use an M3SnackbarHost.

actionLabel.description: Label of the action; omit for a snackbar without one.

x-enumDescriptions.indefinite: Until the action is tapped or the message path is cleared.

message.description: Text to show. Bind it with a path: the host shows what is written there and clears it when the snackbar ends.

modifier.description: Layout and styling modifiers to apply to the host.

onAction.description: Action handler executed when the action was tapped, after the path was cleared.

onDismiss.description: Action handler executed when the snackbar timed out, after the path was cleared.

M3SnackbarHost.description: Material 3 snackbar host: shows the message written to its `message` path as a snackbar, and reports how it ended.
x-invariants: Place it where snackbars should appear, usually the `snackbarHost` of an M3Scaffold. Each host keeps its own state; a second host shows its own messages.

A non-empty message is shown. When the snackbar ends on its own (the duration ran out, or the action was tapped) the host writes an empty string to a bound `message` first, then sends onAction or onDismiss; write the next message after that. A message written while one is shown replaces it: the replaced one writes and sends nothing. An empty message shows nothing and removes a shown one without an event.
With M3SnackbarDuration.Indefinite the snackbar ends only on its action or when the path is cleared. With an actionLabel the action is drawn, and a tap on it ends the snackbar.

formatDate.description: Formats a timestamp into a string using a pattern.

format.description:
A Unicode TR35 date pattern string.

Token Reference:
- Year: 'yy' (26), 'yyyy' (2026)
- Month: 'M' (1), 'MM' (01), 'MMM' (Jan), 'MMMM' (January)
- Day: 'd' (1), 'dd' (01), 'E' (Tue), 'EEEE' (Tuesday)
- Hour (12h): 'h' (1-12), 'hh' (01-12) - requires 'a' for AM/PM
- Hour (24h): 'H' (0-23), 'HH' (00-23) - Military Time
- Minute: 'mm' (00-59)
- Second: 'ss' (00-59)
- Period: 'a' (AM/PM)

Examples:
- 'MMM dd, yyyy' -> 'Jan 16, 2026'
- 'HH:mm' -> '14:30' (Military)
- 'h:mm a' -> '2:30 PM'
- 'EEEE, d MMMM' -> 'Friday, 16 January'

formatString.description: Performs string interpolation of data model values and other functions in the catalog functions list and returns the resulting string. The value string can contain interpolated expressions in the `${expression}` format. Supported expression types include: JSON Pointer paths to the data model (e.g., `${/absolute/path}` or `${relative/path}`), and renderer-side function calls (e.g., `${now()}`). Function arguments must be named (e.g., `${formatDate(value:${/currentDate}, format:'MM-dd')}`). To include a literal `${` sequence, escape it as `\${`. An expression can also be a literal: a quoted string (`'text'` or `"text"`), a number (e.g., `-3.14`), `true` or `false`.

value.description: The template: text with embedded `${expression}` parts, where an expression is a JSON Pointer path, a literal (quoted string, number, `true` or `false`) or a function call with named arguments. Expressions nest, and `\${` is a literal `${`.

instructions: Lay out with M3Column, M3Row and M3Box; group related content in M3Card, M3ElevatedCard or M3OutlinedCard, each with one M3Column. Exactly one component has the id root; other ids are snake_case names (letters, digits, underscores) that say what the component is (users_card, save_button). A container lists its children as an array of ids in content. Bind a value with {"@path": "/user/name"} (RFC 6901, leading slash) and send data in updateDataModel; inputs (M3TextField, M3OutlinedTextField, M3Switch, M3Checkbox, M3Slider) are editable only when value is a path, and write back to it. A button takes its label as a child M3Text and its handler as onClick: {"event": {"name": "save"}}. Prefer M3Button for the main action, M3OutlinedButton or M3TextButton for secondary ones, and M3FAB for one floating action. Give a meaningful M3Icon an accessibility.label. Style with theme tokens, never literal colors: write {"type":"color","value":"primary"} and {"type":"typography","value":"titleMedium"}, not "#6750A4". Leave light and dark to the host, or call setThemeMode. Send a theme only in createSurface or with setTheme, never inside a component; animate only through the theme's motion section.
